query: Our /posts index page issues hundreds of queries and got flagged in a security review. Go through PostController.php and Post.php and tell me exactly what to change and why.
expected_behavior: Fixes the N+1 by eager loading (`Post::with(['author.profile'])`) and replaces `$post->comments->count()` with `withCount('comments')` so comment rows are never hydrated

Recommends making the violation fail loudly instead of relying on review: `Model::preventLazyLoading(! app()->isProduction())` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()`, and names automatic eager loading (`Model::automaticallyEagerLoadRelationships()` / `withRelationshipAutoloading()`) as the alternative strategy rather than mixing both

Calls out `$guarded = []` as the mass-assignment hole and pairs it with `$request->validated()` / `safe()->only([...])` instead of `$request->all()`, noting `user_id` is currently settable by the client
Fixes the `search` method: the interpolated `$term` is SQL injection and the interpolated `$direction` cannot be fixed by a binding at all, so it must be mapped through an allow-list
Adds a `datetime` cast for `published_at` (and moves casts into a `casts()` method) rather than parsing the raw string in the controller or view

Points out that `scopeForCurrentTeam` reads `auth()->user()` inside the model, so the scope breaks in queue jobs, Artisan commands and tests where there is no authenticated user - the tenant should be passed in
Notes that `export()` loads every post and issues one UPDATE per row, and replaces it with chunked iteration keyed on the primary key (`chunkById` / `lazyById`) or a single bulk update

query: Warehouse sync duplicates shipments after a deploy, some orders get synced for a transaction we rolled back, and the failure log always says '0 attempts'. Here is the job, the service that dispatches it and the queue config. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the reservation race: the connection's `retry_after` (90s) is shorter than the job/worker timeout (300s), so a second worker reserves and re-runs a job that is still executing - `retry_after` must exceed the longest timeout, and the worker `--timeout` must stay below `retry_after`

Says the job must be made idempotent regardless of the timeout fix (an idempotency key on the outbound POST, or a check of `warehouse_reference` before posting), because a worker can die after the side effect and before acknowledging

Explains that `SyncOrderToWarehouse::dispatch($order)` inside `DB::transaction` can be picked up before the transaction commits, and fixes it with `afterCommit()` on the dispatch or `'after_commit' => true` on the connection - and applies the same reasoning to the event and the queued notification

Explains that `failed()` runs on a freshly deserialised job instance, so `$this->attemptLog` is always empty there; use `$this->attempts()` or the passed exception instead of state mutated during `handle()`
Notes that the outbound HTTP call has no explicit `connectTimeout`/`timeout` and does not check the response (`->throw()` or an explicit status check) before reading `reference` from the body
Recommends `ShouldBeUnique` with a `uniqueId` for dispatch-level deduplication while stating that it is a cache lock, not a substitute for idempotent processing

Uses the Laravel 13 attribute form (`#[Tries]`, `#[Backoff]`, `#[Timeout]`) or explicitly says the public `$tries`/`$timeout` properties remain supported, and does not declare both for the same setting

query: This Pest file is flaky on CI - the 'express-checkout' test fails about one run in three, and the first test passes even when checkout is broken. AppServiceProvider.php has the flag definition. Fix the tests and tell me what is actually wrong.
expected_behavior: Identifies the real cause of the flag flakiness: Pennant stores the resolved value the first time a feature is checked for a scope, so a `Lottery` gives a per-user coin flip that the test cannot control - the test must re-define the feature (`Feature::define('express-checkout', true)`) or activate it for the scope under test

Says that editing the odds in the service provider does not change values already stored, so a rollout change needs `Feature::purge('express-checkout')` / `php artisan pennant:purge` in the deployment

Rewrites the first test into a real assertion: a name that states the result, plus assertions on the persisted state and dispatched side effects rather than `assertStatus(200)` followed by `expect(true)->toBeTrue()`
Moves the factory records out of `beforeEach()` into the tests that use them, so each test states its own data and can pick its own factory state
Replaces `Carbon::setTestNow()` with the framework helpers `freezeTime()` / `travelTo()`

Replaces the bare `Http::fake()` with `Http::preventStrayRequests()` plus a fake for the specific endpoint, and points out that `Event::fake()` with no class names both hides unexpected dispatches and suppresses model events used by factories

Uses named response assertions (`assertOk()`, `assertForbidden()`) instead of `assertStatus(...)`, and notes that a cross-tenant request usually should answer 404 rather than 403 so it does not confirm the record exists

Keeps a status assertion (`assertOk()`) beside `assertSee('Express checkout')` in the rollout test, because `assertSee` only searches the body and would also pass on an error page that contains the text
Mentions test-suite hygiene that applies here: `LazilyRefreshDatabase` instead of `RefreshDatabase`, and low `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` in the testing environment

query: ImportLedgerStatement.php is one of our queue jobs (Laravel 13.34, Redis queue, three worker hosts). ledger-worker.log shows what happens on large statements and has our worker .env. We want a statement that keeps crashing the worker to give up after three bad attempts, the same as real exceptions do, but we need to keep the 25 tries because the WithoutOverlapping lock releases the job a lot. What is going on, and what exactly should change?
expected_behavior: Explains that an attempt killed by the OOM killer (SIGKILL) never throws inside handle(), so `MaxExceptions(3)` never counts it; each crash only consumes a try, which is why the job cycled until `Tries(25)` ran out with MaxAttemptsExceededException

Adds `#[CountCrashesAsExceptions]` (Illuminate\Queue\Attributes, available from Laravel 13.34) next to `#[MaxExceptions(3)]` so a crashed attempt counts toward the exception limit while `#[Tries(25)]` stays for lock releases - instead of lowering Tries or hand-rolling a crash counter in the cache or a middleware

Says the exception counter and the crash marker (and the WithoutOverlapping lock) live in the worker's default cache store, so `CACHE_STORE=file` on three hosts counts and locks per host; the workers need a shared store such as Redis or the database

Fixes the memory cause: stream the CSV (SplFileObject/fgetcsv or a LazyCollection) and insert in chunks or batches instead of `file()` plus `array_map` holding the whole statement and one `create()` per row

query: We still oversell seats for popular events, a few times a week, always when PayHub is having a slow day - even though every reservation goes through the cache lock in SeatReservationService.php. Redis is shared by all six web hosts. Find the cause and give me the corrected service.
expected_behavior: Identifies that the lock's 5-second lease is shorter than the callback can run (a 20-second response timeout across up to three attempts, plus connect timeouts and retry sleeps), so on a slow PayHub day the lock expires mid-callback, a second request acquires it and reads the old `seats_remaining`, and both decrement - and states that the lease must exceed the worst-case duration of the locked work, derived from those timeouts, not its typical duration

Makes the decrement safe in the database instead of trusting the cache lock alone - a `lockForUpdate()` re-read inside the transaction, or an atomic conditional decrement (`where('seats_remaining', '>=', $seats)` plus `decrement()` and a check of the affected rows) - because `seats_remaining - $seats` computed from an earlier read loses updates whenever two writers overlap

Shrinks what the lock covers by taking the slow external authorisation out of the critical section (or otherwise bounding it), and handles the seats running out after the card was authorised by voiding or releasing that authorisation

query: A subscriber wrote in that she was unsubscribed from our newsletter and her topics were changed, but she never clicked anything. Every newsletter link is a signed URL (newsletter-routes.php shows the routes and how the mail builds the links) and the signed middleware is on all of them, so we assumed nobody could act on someone else's subscription. Review NewsletterController.php, explain how this could happen, and fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that the signature covers only the URL path and query string, while `$request->input()`, `$request->all()`, `validate()` and dynamic request properties merge the request body over the query string, so anyone holding their own valid signed link can send a form or JSON body (even on the GET unsubscribe route) with another subscriber's `email` and act on that subscriber

Reads the identity that was signed from the query string only - `$request->query('email')` (or a route parameter that is part of the signed URL) - in both actions, instead of trusting the merged input or adding more validation to the `email` field
Keeps the preferences fields (`frequency`, `topics`) as ordinary validated body input but removes `email` from the validated body, so the update is keyed only on the signed value
Adds or describes a test that sends a validly signed link for one subscriber with a different `email` in the request body and asserts the other subscriber is unchanged

query: Today is 1 November 2026. Our field-service app is on Laravel 12 (composer.json). The product owner wants to push the Laravel 13 upgrade back to Q2 2027 and asks whether Laravel 12 keeps getting fixes until then. Answer that with dates, and give me the upgrade plan, including what has to happen before the framework bump itself.
expected_behavior: States that Laravel 12's bug-fix window has already closed (13 August 2026) and it now gets security fixes only, ending 24 February 2027, so postponing to Q2 2027 leaves the application on an unsupported framework and the upgrade has to land before late February 2027

Notes that Laravel 13 requires PHP 8.3 or newer while composer.json allows `^8.2` and pins `config.platform.php` to 8.2.29, so the PHP runtime and the platform pin move to 8.3+ first, before the framework bump

Raises the dependency floors together - `laravel/framework ^13.0`, `laravel/tinker ^3.0`, Pest 4 with its Laravel plugin - and checks the third-party packages (spatie/laravel-permission, sanctum) for Laravel 13 support before switching

Plans the work on a dedicated branch from a clean tree with the current checks green first, one revertable change per commit, and works through the 12-to-13 breaking changes (for example the CSRF middleware's rename to PreventRequestForgery and the cache `serializable_classes` default)
